title: Plural of selected longer words: -oita/-öitä
summary: For these selected longer words, form the taught -oita/-öitä plural: peruna (“potato”) → perunoita.
objectives: Form the plural partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

These selected longer nouns use -oita/-öitä. For peruna, replace final -a with -oita. For the selected -kka/-kko/-kkä words, the -oita/-öitä form uses one k: replace -kka/-kko with -koita and -kkä with -köitä. These latter words also allow a standard alternative with kk and -oja/-öjä; both taught forms are accepted in typed production. These are selected families, not a rule for every longer word.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Replace final -a with -oita: peruna → perunoita. The standard alternatives perunia and perunoja are also accepted; they replace -a with -ia and -oja respectively.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “potato”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Replace -kka with -koita: mansikka → mansikoita. Alternatively replace -a with -oja and retain kk: mansikkoja.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “strawberry”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Replace -kka with -koita: lusikka → lusikoita. Alternatively replace -a with -oja and retain kk: lusikkoja.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “spoon”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Replace -kko with -koita: laatikko → laatikoita. Alternatively add -ja to the dictionary form: laatikkoja.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “box”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Replace -kkä with -köitä: kännykkä → kännyköitä. Alternatively replace -ä with -öjä and retain kk: kännykköjä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “mobile phone”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Use one k with -oita/-öitä in this selected kk family.
Do not generalize this lesson to all three-syllable words.
